problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 4 \\ 3 & -4 & 10 \\ 2 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 \\ -5 & -4 & -6 \\ 2 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?

examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071806/assets/941de9bd4837b4b5c9f0d2bf64c4ea0fd9be657b0368d03cac169742083822d1.png)

By applying elementary column operations of the form $C_i:=C_i+kC_3,$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
examples.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left of $a_{13}={\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}}$ equal to ${\color{red}0}.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & -5 & 1 \\ 8 & 3 & -4 \\ 9 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+6{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 & 1 \\ -16 & 3 & -4 \\ -3 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+5{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ -16 & -17 & -4 \\ -3 & -3 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\qquad$ $C_1:=C_1+6C_3\quad$ and $\quad C_2:=C_2+5C_3.$

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-17 & 8 & 0 & 7 \\ -7 & 4 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & -4 & 5 & -2 \\ 6 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 4 & 3 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 3 \\ -7 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 6 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{1}:=…$
- ${R}_{2}:=…$
- ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-2{R}_{4}$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{4},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
feedback.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above ${a}_{42}=-2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-17 & 8 & 0 & 7 \\ -7 & 4 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & -4 & 5 & -2 \\ 6 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+4{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 4 & 3 \\ -7 & 4 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & -4 & 5 & -2 \\ 6 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 4 & 3 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 3 \\ 5 & -4 & 5 & -2 \\ 6 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-2{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 4 & 3 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 3 \\ -7 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 6 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+4{R}_{4}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{4}.$
